messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate parameters. The user wants weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius. We need to find latitude and longitude for White Plains. White Plains is a city in New York, USA. Coordinates: approx 41.0535° N, 73.7629° W. So latitude 41.0535, longitude -73.7629. We want forecast for next week. The Open-Meteo API supports daily forecast. We can request daily parameters like temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min. We need to set timezone. For White Plains, timezone is America/New_York. We also need to specify start_date and end_date. Next week: from tomorrow to 7 days ahead? Let's assume next 7 days starting from tomorrow. We need to get today's date. Today is 2026-07-16. Next week would be 2026-07-17 to 2026-07-23. We'll set start_date=2026-07-17, end_date=2026-07-23. Also we need to set daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min. And we want units in Celsius. The API returns in Celsius by default. But we can specify "temperature_unit=celsius". Actually the API uses "temperature_unit" param. Let's check. The Open-Meteo API has parameter "temperature_unit" which can be "celsius" or "fahrenheit". We'll set "temperature_unit": "celsius". Also "windspeed_unit" etc. But we only need temperature. So we set "daily": "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min". Also "timezone": "America/New_York". Also "forecast_days" maybe not needed. We'll just use start_date and end_date.

Thus the function call:

{
  "url": "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
  "params": {
    "latitude": 41.0535,
    "longitude": -73.7629,
    "start_date": "2026-07-17",
    "end_date": "2026-07-23",
    "daily": "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min",
    "timezone": "America/New_York",
    "temperature_unit": "celsius"
  }
}

We don't need headers. We'll use default. So let's call the function.
